rationale.conceptual: The paper applies a standard NEMD technique with the GAFF force field and Fourier's law extrapolation. No novel algorithms or deep theoretical derivations are required; it is a textbook application of MD to a new material.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves building multiple crystal orientations and interface configurations, running many NEMD simulations (size-dependent, TBR, vacancy), and performing linear extrapolation. While each step is straightforward, coordinating up to 20+ independent simulations and correctly parsing outputs constitutes a multi-stage orchestration with dependencies.

difficulty.reasoning: The task reproduces established non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) simulations using a standard force field (GAFF) and the LAMMPS package, applied to a specific organic crystal. The method is well-documented and widely used; the main challenge is careful execution of a multi-stage pipeline of MD runs and post-processing. The conceptual novelty is low, but engineering many simulation runs warrants moderate execution difficulty.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Simulation boxes contain a few thousand atoms; NEMD runs last nanoseconds per length. Entire workflow can run on a few CPU cores with modest memory. No GPU acceleration is required; input data (crystal structure, force field) is negligible.
